blocks.text: Persistent organic pollutants are organic compounds resistant to degradation by chemical, biological and photolytic processes. They are toxic, harm human health and the environment, and travel by wind and water, so POPs generated in one country can affect people and wildlife far from where they were used and released. Because they persist they accumulate in the environment and can have significant adverse effects on health (Table 14.1).

blocks.caption: Some POPs and their uses (Table 14.1)
rows: electrical equipment, surface coatings, inks, adhesives and paints

blocks.prompt: What are the environmental impacts of persistent organic pollutants (exercise Q.2e)?
blocks.explanation: Because they resist chemical, biological and photochemical breakdown, POPs such as PCBs and DDT persist for years, are carried by wind and water across borders, and build up in soils, water and the fatty tissues of animals along food chains, poisoning wildlife and people far from their source.

items: POPs resist degradation, are toxic, travel far by wind and water and accumulate: PCBs (electrical equipment, paints), DDT (insecticide).
